newsitem.title: FRANCE: Deficit cuts essential - Bank of France's Trichet.
newsitem.headline: Deficit cuts essential - Bank of France's Trichet.

text.p: Bank of France chief Jean-Claude Trichet said on Tuesday that it was essential to make cuts in the public deficits in 1997.
Presenting the bank's annual report at a news conference, Trichet said: "Reducing public deficits is indispensible in 1997 as it is in the medium term."

Trichet said France's payroll deductions to fund the welfare system were too high and public spending must also fall. Trichet stressed the report was written before the new Socialist-led government announced its policy programme last week and did not constitute a response to it.

He called for continuing wage restraint and said the ratio of public spending to gross domestic product of 54.5 percent was "manifestly too high" and should be reduced gradually and substantially to the European Union (EU) average of 49.9 percent.
Trichet said monetary policy had brought French market interest rates to historic lows but was not sufficient to fight unemployment, which required structural reforms and sustained deficit reduction.

He said market interest rates were low because the franc was stable and credible and vowed the Bank of France would continue its action in 1997-98 to ensure that the euro inspired as much confidence as the franc.
